answer.rationale: Rollback is precluded by compliance since the release contains a mandatory security patch, so memory_b1 is not actionable despite matching the symptom pattern. The dominant driver right now is heavy write volume at daily settlement peak causing p99 climb on the write path; memory_b3 documents that provisioning headroom before a traffic peak kept queue depth flat, which directly targets sustained write availability without touching the protected release or customer writes. Read-replica routing (b5) mainly offloads read/report traffic and won't relieve write-path latency; circuit breakers (b4) protect against a failing dependency, not generalized load-driven latency; regional failover (b2) is a heavier, riskier shift when the cause looks like capacity rather than a regional outage. Given severity (5x target, 90 minutes sustained, peak settlement writes) and that only one intervention fits in this window, a broad capacity addition is warranted rather than a small guarded test, but I flag downstream value risk since added capacity has cost/resource tradeoffs and does not fully rule out a release-induced contribution to latency that cannot be addressed this window.
